| identity | `required-open` | A motion is first-order data: a list of tracks, each a key, a change of one kind and a transition. An easing is a list of stops or the two heights of a cubic, in per mille. A frame is a value for each of the five properties of a thing. No function is stored. | construction | `required-open` | A step's motion is built from the join of two pictures and a plan: what a kept thing does, how a new thing enters and how an old one leaves. A motion is then held in its step, started later thing by thing, put after another, fitted to a length, reduced to its ends, or put in stages: the kept things first, then the new things level by level, each level in a slot of its own. Open: nothing in the type of a motion says that a thing has one track at most for a property: `Motion.Single` says it as a predicate, and it is proved of the step of a plan that changes no property twice (`Motion.single_ofJoin`); a motion that a caller builds by hand has no such proof. | semantics | `required-open` | `Track.at` is the meaning of a track: the pose of a thing at a moment, by the easing of the share of the duration that has passed, with one rounding down. `Motion.frame` is the meaning of a motion for one thing: its poses put on the still picture in the order of the tracks, a later pose of one property in place of an earlier one. `Join.drawn` says which things a reader draws at a moment of a step. `Transition.exact` and `mixExact` are the same readings in rational numbers at a rational time, and the whole-number readings are their floors. Open: the exact reading is stated at every rational time, for a value, a gap and a kept relation: no law speaks of a real time or of a limit, and a size that grows past its end has no exact form; a frame does not know a thing's own shape: `Frame.AtRest` says nothing of the shape, and a thing whose shape a track changed keeps the last one given; of a step it is known under a premise (`Step.frame_shape`: a thing of the new picture has its own shape at every moment where the plan changes no shape); a thing inside a group that moves has its own frame and its group's, and no function puts the one inside the other. | laws | `required-open` | The end law: a track whose transition is over stands at the end of its change, so a step's last moment is the next picture, and with a plan that settles every thing of the new list then looks as the still picture has it. Between the two pictures: a kept edge that changes its shape by its nodes' transition stays joined to them, and a relation of both pictures is a relation of every whole moment, and of every rational time in exact numbers, where the things share one timing and the easing stays in range. In time: a delay by depth, a fit to a length, a reduction to the ends and a step in stages each keep the order that the tracks had, and in a staged step no new thing appears before the kept things are at rest. Of a thing: where no thing has two tracks of one property, its frame shows the pose of each of its tracks and does not depend on their order. Of a whole step: kept things that take one transition with an easing in range keep, where they stand at every moment, each relation that their places have in both pictures. Of an interruption: at the first moment of a step that resumes from where things are seen, each kept thing shows every pose that it showed and stands where it stood, and the step ends on the next picture. Open: a fact of an easing at whole stops does not reach a transition of a duration other than a thousand, and the duration that a distance asks for has no law of order (debt D126); no law says that a thing that leaves ends as nothing: a plan's `leave` may be any change; `Motion.Same` is kept by `++` in its second part only where both rows are `Single`: the law without that premise is false, and an example of `Frame.lean` refutes it; a step in stages has no order inside one level: with lean4-effect4's shares a new edge and the box at its end overlap by a twentieth of the slot; a step resumed with speed (`Plan.springResume`) keeps the gaps of its pictures in exact places only (`Spring.critical_followed_gap`): each thing then takes an easing of its own, so `Motion.together` does not reach its whole-number frames, and the law waits for a change through way points or for shifts that add (debt D134); a step in stages that interrupts another has no law of its first moment: `Track.endBy` rounds a short duration to nothing (control in `Whatwg/Svg/Scene/Step/Laws.lean`); no law of frames says that a new thing of a staged step is not seen before its level; the law of the kept things of a step is of two kept things at whole moments: a kept thing against a new or a leaving one, and the same law at a rational time, are not stated for a step. | representation | `required-open` | An easing of two heights is the curve that CSS names `cubic-bezier(1/3, y1, 2/3, y2)`, whose first coordinate is the progress, and the reading of a transition is that polynomial at the exact share of the duration, rounded down once. A list of stops is what CSS names `linear(…)`. The writer gives each change under each easing one rule of two keyframes with the easing in it, and each track a duration and a delay, filled both ways; its times are written exactly, to a thousandth of a millisecond; a step can be opened at a moment, running or paused, or at the moment that a custom property says; and the sheet can end every animation at once for a reader who asks for reduced motion. Since slice S17 the sheet and a thing's declarations are data before they are text (`Whatwg/Html/Node/Css.lean`). Open: no law relates the written sheet to the reading: CSS animations, CSS easing functions, the individual transform properties and `d` as a property are not sealed, and the package holds no model of what a browser computes from them; debt D119.
